title: Incident Relay Lane: Foldable Timeline Actions and SLO-Aware Handoff Notes
creator: Marisa Chen
description:
Problem: On high-urgency incidents engineers repeatedly lose time locating the right runbook snippet, SLO snapshot, and postmortem link during a handoff. Existing alert cards are modal-heavy and require multiple clicks to gather context for the next on-call person.

Goal: Design a compact, contextual ‘Incident Relay Lane’ attached to each alert timeline entry that surfaces stepwise actions, a minimal SLO snapshot, and sticky handoff notes (copyable) so handoffs are faster and fewer critical details are missed. Keep the surface low-visual-weight so it doesn't dominate the incident timeline.

Scope: Console timeline UI only (desktop first). Includes: the Relay Lane UI pattern, micro-interactions for folding/unfolding actions, copy-to-clipboard for runbook snippets, quicklinks to the postmortem and retrospective, and an SLO delta mini-sparkline specific to the alert window. Does not include backend or RBAC changes (those are in ENG-4821).

Design principles and constraints: prioritize speed of comprehension, minimal clicks (<=2 to hand off core info), keyboard-first access for paging through Relay Lanes, and clear affordances for copying/linking. Must work with existing timeline density and accessible at 14px+ font sizes.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Collapsible rail appended to each timeline event: collapsed shows a 44px tall summary strip (icon + SLO delta + 1-line action hint).
- Expandable lane slides up inline to reveal 3 primary columns: (1) actionable steps (ordered list with one-click 'mark done' toggles), (2) one-click copy runbook snippet with inline edit, (3) postmortem & retrospective quicklinks + stakeholder ping button.
- SLO snapshot: 3 small datapoints (error rate, latency percentile, burn rate) + a 12–24hr mini-sparkline derived from console metrics. Clicking the snapshot opens the SLO panel.
- Handoff note: field pinned at top of expanded lane. Editable by current oncall. Automatically saved to incident journal and shown as a highlighted timeline entry when updated.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype allows user to copy a runbook snippet and paste into Slack in <=6s after opening the lane.
- Handoff note saves and appears as a timeline entry within 10s.
- User testing (n=6 engineers) shows preferred flow in 5/6 sessions vs current baseline.

Deliverables attached: Figma prototype links, interaction spec, accessibility checklist, and a short usability test script.
activity:
2025-02-21: Initial sketch and low-fi mockups completed. Shared with PM (Diego Alvarez) for alignment on telemetry.

2025-02-24: Design critique with Eng (Sofia Patel, Aman Kaur). Key feedback: make SLO snapshot data readonly (do not allow inline edits), surface only one primary CTA to avoid decision paralysis, and ensure expand animation does not reflow timeline content. Action: update prototype to overlay-expand pattern.

2025-02-27: Usability test plan drafted. Target participants: 6 oncall engineers across infra and runtime teams. Tasks: perform handoff, copy runbook, and link postmortem. Metrics: time-on-task, error rate, qualitative confidence score.

2025-03-01: PM review (Diego): request to add a lightweight toggle to automatically include checklist items in handoff note. Design decision: add optional pinned checklist that can be templated per project (future work).

2025-03-03: Design review scheduled with Product and Research. Updated prototype uploaded (see attachments). Notes from review: accessibility OK at 14px but confirm color contrast for the SLO sparkline; engineering flagged API payload size concerns for autosave frequency (ENG-4821). Next steps: (1) finalize interaction spec, (2) hand off to ENG for feasibility sprint, (3) run small moderated usability session week of 2025-03-10.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: embedding too much information increases cognitive load; we chose a progressive disclosure model with a compact summary + optional expanded details. We intentionally limited the number of primary actions to three to reduce noisy decision paths.

Open questions:
- Should the handoff note be auto-suggested from the incident timeline events? (product TBD)
- Template management UX for pinned checklists (scope creep risk).

Follow-ups: ENG to provide a rough estimate for autosave cadence and attachments size (ENG-4821). PM to confirm retention policy for handoff notes in the incident journal. Research to run A/B with current baseline using same tasks.
